text:
devon: quick summary of the livepipe experiment i ran this morning (SSE vs websocket vs short-poll HTTP). ran on us-west1 (H100) and eu-central1 (A100). smallish prompt mix (avg 120 tokens), bursty arrivals.
maria: nice — top-line numbers?
devon: benchbot posted the runs but TL;DR:
- WebSocket streaming: best p50 latency (40–60ms per token) and highest steady throughput when persistent connections open, p99 ~420ms for first token in burst.
- SSE streaming: similar to websocket for single-connection flows but ~10% worse CPU on gateway (node nginx) and higher reconnect churn in eu region.
- Non-streaming (HTTP chunked / single-response): lower tail for end-to-end completion on short outputs (p50 120ms) but much higher per-request CPU and worse throughput under high concurrency — saturates at ~60% fewer T/second.
ajay: can you paste exact numbers (RPS, tokens/s, p50/p95/p99)?
devon: sure, run averaged over 3 runs each (90s windows), synthetic client with 1000 clients, backlog ramp:
```csv
mode,gpu_region,gpu_type,conns,requests/s,tokens/s,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms
ws,us-west1,H100,1000,2200,264000,45,220,420
sse,us-west1,H100,1000,2000,240000,55,260,480
http,us-west1,H100,1000,1400,168000,120,480,820
ws,eu-central1,A100,1000,1800,216000,60,280,600
sse,eu-central1,A100,1000,1600,192000,68,320,720
http,eu-central1,A100,1000,1000,120000,150,520,950
```
lina: interesting delta between regions — likely due to kernel selection and PCIe topology differences on the cluster images.
devon: yep. we saw that H100 runs picked optimized flash-attn kernels and int8 quant paths; A100 fallback picked generic kernels leading to ~15–20% throughput loss for streaming steady-state.
maria: what about batching / batching window? did you force continuous batching or single-token flush on stream?
devon: streaming used continuous batching with max_batch 32 and a small 8ms hold window. Non-streaming used request-level batching with max_batch 64 and 12ms hold. When we increased hold window to 20ms, throughput went up ~8% but p50 increased by ~5–8ms — tradeoff curve expected.
ajay: any regressions from recent quantization changes?
devon: int4 experimental quant gave ~1.1x tokens/s on H100 in non-stream mode but slightly higher p99 jitter for first tokens on streaming (cache warmup + decoding scheduling). we flagged it to perf and mlops teams.
benchbot: job 1859987600 complete — 3 trials each, 95% CI +/- 2.7% on tokens/s.
maria: what are the operational notes? e.g., backpressure, client reconnect behavior for SSE vs WS?
devon: SSE had simpler reconnection semantics but we hit a bug in nginx proxy where idle keepalive dropped at 60s causing reconnect storms. WS preserved connection better under our gateway (envoy) and allowed per-connection rate limiting. Important: streaming endpoints require sticky LB + long-lived connection tuning (tcp_fin_timeout, keepalive) otherwise you pay huge p99s.
lina: capacity sizing recommendation?
devon: for our workload (avg 120 tokens, 5% long tail >800 tokens):
- Prefer websocket streaming for high-concurrency low-latency workloads; size by sustained tokens/s with headroom (1.5x) to handle spikes.
- Use non-streaming for batch/offline or short, low-concurrency calls to simplify infra.
- For Dedicated pools: prefer H100 for streaming-critical models; A100 is fine but bump node count ~1.2x for parity.
ajay: any immediate actions?
devon: created a short playbook and a perf ticket:
- patch nginx keepalive config in eu cluster (ops: #3214)
- add kernel hinting for A100 images (eng-runtime)
- run int4 stability bench with larger prompt variety (ml-evals)
maria: can you drop the playbook link here?
devon: link: https://internal.redwood/charts/livepipe/1859 and playbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/streaming-sizing
lina: thanks, this is actionable. i’ll take ops ticket for nginx.
ajay: i’ll follow up on kernel hints and quant bench.
devon: thanks — let me know if you want raw logs, I have the perf traces + flame graphs attached in the chart page. :thumbsup:
